newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Suspicious Swiss guard gives Jews bank documents.
newsitem.headline: Suspicious Swiss guard gives Jews bank documents.

text.p: A suspicious security guard at Switzerland's biggest bank stole old documents bound for the shredder and gave them to Swiss Jews in the belief they could help the search for Holocaust funds, the bank said on Tuesday.

Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) acknowledged the plan to shred the wartime-era documents was a clear violation of the government's ban on destroying any material that could be important in the search for dormant Jewish accounts.
But it denied the documents were related in any way to dormant accounts. Jewish groups have alleged Swiss banks are still hoarding billions of dollars in Nazi victims' wealth.
"UBS strongly regrets the incident," it said in a statement, noting the employee had also violated the bank's own blanket ban on destroying any documents.
A UBS spokesman said the documents were purely historical in nature and of no relevance to the search for lost Jewish money.
"There were no client documents," she said, adding: "In principle the documents and the Holocaust debate have nothing to do with each other."
Zurich prosecutors are investigating the matter.
The documents relate to the Eidgenoessische Bank, a bank that UBS acquired in the 1940s.

A UBS employee had been searching through the bank's files and released some of the documents which he considered unimportant for shredding. They included minutes of meetings, annual reports and other such documents, the spokeswoman said.
The security guard, however, discovered and removed these documents from UBS last week and handed them over to Zurich's Jewish community, which then contacted Zurich prosecutors.

UBS said it was cooperating with prosecutors, but its own investigation showed the employee had no intention of destroying documents that could be of use in the inquiry into Swiss relations with Nazi Germany during World War Two.

The Swiss government last month banned the destruction of any documents that could be used in the probe. It has agreed to lift banking secrecy for dormant accounts and let an international panel of historians conduct a review.
